title: Gratitude Volume and Mood Link
dataSources: Prayer sessions (`prayer:session`), scripture readings (`scripture:reading`), fasting logs (`fasting:log`), gratitude entries (`gratitude:entry`), retreats (`retreat:event`).
app: Spiritual-practice and mindfulness logs — prayer / meditation timers, scripture-reading plans (YouVersion), fasting and gratitude journals, and retreat calendars — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=gratitude:entry
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as entries, avg(mood) as mood by _time
| eval volume=if(entries>=3,"3+ entries","1-2 entries")
| stats avg(mood) as avg_mood, count as days by volume
description: Compares your mood on days you wrote lots of gratitude notes against days you wrote only one or two.
value: Seeing your own gratitude-mood link, in your own data, is far more convincing than being told it works.
implementation: Ingest gratitude entries with a mood score into `index=personal`; compare mood by how much you journaled.
visualization: Bar chart of average mood by gratitude-journaling volume.

references.title: Greater Good Science Center — gratitude research

grandmaExplanation: It compares how you felt on days you counted many blessings versus few, showing gratitude's effect.
